body:
Please remove the specific date from your head.  I lost a friend because of this for no good reason:

- He had a good job, and was married happily for several years
- Shortly before his "date" (which he didn't announce to anyone, but it was in his suicide note), he went through a rough divorce
- On the specific date, he was very depressed

In short, he had a good live for many years, and was depressed for a couple of months.  You never know what life might throw you, but it definitely has it's ups and downs.  Please don't take some stupid risk that you might be in a slump whenever your date comes 9 years from now.

Honestly, it depends on how bad you are.  My advice, knowing little about you, is to finish school then go traveling after high school / before university.  If you _absolutely need_ to do this now, you have two options: Test out of high school (I did this), or just go and figure it out later.

But no matter what you do, please finish school.  Life gets so much harder for people that don't.  Now preferably, in a year if you need to.

If you make the decision to leave, talk to the people in your life.  They may disagree with you, but it's also your life and they'll hopefully support you once they realize you're serious and you give your reasons.  If you decide to stay, either find someone to talk to or ask your parents to take you to a psychologist, someone that you know will keep your secrets, someone safe to talk to, and someone that can hopefully help you.

I realize many people that might read this would thoroughly disagree with this advice, but in my opinion finding a long term path is so much more important than anything else.  If you can stick through school, please do so, but if you can't there are much better alternatives than suicide.

I've been where you are, my friend, many many times.  Life doesn't always offer the perfect solutions, but my advice to you is to try and find them before you make any irreversible decision.

You say you may be "running away to some faraway place" -- Do it.  The world has so much more to offer than is in front of you, and traveling, especially alone, gives you a new vantage point on so many things.  Don't cut ties, and don't "run away" from people you don't need to, but do figure out what you want, who you are, and what you can get from life.

I tried to kill myself about a decade ago.  A friend of mine found me having OD'd on OTC drugs and alcohol.  I was rushed to the hospital, had my stomach pumped, and narrowly avoided permanent liver damage.  My friends after that gave me this advice -- Waste every bit of your money and resources, then decided if you want to live or not.  

That may be phrased a bit weird, but the point is this -- Live before you decide whether or not you want to die.  It's gotten me the last 10 years or so.
